quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How can you lower your risk of being in a crash?

options.text: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Ride in parts of the lane where you are hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, always make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your bike and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Which surface does NOT have poor traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor traction. Wet roads, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings are all more dangerous than dry pavement for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Before riding, make sure your brakes:

options.text: Can each hold the motorcycle still.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can each hold the motorcycle still.
questions.explanation: Check each brake lever before every ride. Both the front and rear brakes should feel firm and be able to hold your motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: You should wear a jacket when riding a motorcycle:

options.text: Only on rides longer than 30 minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: In all weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and helps prevent dehydration.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, be ready for:

options.text: A parked car to suddenly pull into traffic.
Other drivers to see you and stay away.

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car to suddenly pull into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may pull out suddenly into traffic. It is safer to ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on the right. This gives you more space between your bike and any hazards.

questions.question: The best lane position is the one that:

options.text: Lets you follow closely behind other vehicles.
Makes other drivers able to see you.
Puts you in other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes other drivers able to see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind, blind spots, and road hazards. It also stops other drivers from trying to share your lane and gives you a way to escape danger. Choose a position that gives you the most space.

questions.question: At an intersection, you can be seen better by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Riding with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Use your headlight to increase visibility at intersections. Ride in a position where oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep space around your bike so you can take action if needed.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
Does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A helmet will not limit your vision. Any U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet will give you the side vision you need to ride safely.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Trust that everything on your bike works.
Check your bike before every ride.
Check your bike once a month.
Check your bike twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your bike before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small mechanical problem on a motorcycle is more serious than on a car. Check your bike thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: Your best source for information about your motorcycle is:
questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It explains how to operate it, its features, and what maintenance it needs.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: How can motorcycle riders help others see them?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to increase visibility. Also use your headlight at all times and always use your turn signals.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Are not helpful since you can't do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of normal driving. Also check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: What is important to know about motorcycle blind spots?

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots that are too small to cause any problems.
Have blind spots that require head checks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that require head checks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you're planning to increase your speed.
Only when there is a lot of traffic.
Any time you plan on changing lanes.
Only if it is dark outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan on changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?
questions.correctAnswerText: THC
questions.explanation: THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) is the main active ingredient in marijuana.

questions.question: What benefit do gloves provide to motorcycle riders?

options.text: Make it difficult to control a motorcycle and should be avoided.
Provide an improved grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide an improved grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: Have brakes in both the front and rear.
Have three brakes: one in the front, one in the rear, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: What happens if you take a corner too fast?

options.text: Can cause the rider to go into another lane.
Is better than going too slowly.
Often causes the rider to stay in their lane.
Is acceptable because motorcycles are smaller than other types of vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause the rider to go into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before turning.

questions.question: What is the best source of information about your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who owns a different type of motorcycle
A television show about motorcycle riding

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual
questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before you ride it for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. The manual explains how your specific motorcycle works.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective clothes
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing. This makes it easier for other drivers to see you and your motorcycle on the road.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you
No, clothing is just a personal choice
Yes, but only if the clothes are very loose and flap in the wind
Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely
questions.explanation: The right clothing reduces injury in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants made of sturdy material that cover your arms and legs completely. The clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.

questions.question: To protect a motorcycle rider, pants should be:

options.text: Loose enough to flap in the wind

questions.correctAnswerText: Made of a heavy material
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. The pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: What should you look for when choosing a protective jacket or pants?
questions.correctAnswerText: Items made of leather
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and long pants that cover your arms and legs completely while riding. Leather clothing provides the highest level of protection.
